ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The Lorentz force demonstration instrument in physics classroom teaching consists of an excitation coil, a glass bulb, an electron gun, and other parts. The excitation coil is a pair of mutually parallel coaxial circular coils, which can produce a uniform magnetic field between the two coils. The glass bulb is filled with thin gas. The electron gun emits electrons under an accelerating voltage, and when the electron beam passes through the gas inside the bulb, it can show the trajectory of electron motion. If the electron gun emits electrons perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, after energizing the excitation coil, one can see that the trajectory of the electron beam is circular. If only the accelerating voltage of the electron gun or the current in the excitation coil is increased, which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.title: The influence of excitation coil current on orbital radius
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In this Lorentz force demonstration instrument, if the emission direction of the electron gun is always perpendicular to the magnetic field, and other conditions remain unchanged, when only the current in the excitation coil is increased, how does the radius of the electron beam's circular orbit change?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that this device is a Lorentz force demonstration instrument, containing an excitation coil, a glass bulb, and an electron gun; the electron beam forms a circular trajectory in the glass bulb, indicating that when the electron emission direction is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the Lorentz force provides the centripetal force. The hypothesis requires that other conditions remain unchanged and only the current in the excitation coil is increased. Increasing the excitation coil current will increase the magnetic induction intensity B produced by the coil; since other conditions such as the accelerating voltage remain unchanged, the electron speed v remains unchanged. With the Lorentz force providing the centripetal force: qvB = mv^2/r, one can obtain r = mv/(qB). Therefore when v remains unchanged, B increases, and the orbital radius r decreases.
